chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala and Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the mines of gold, silver, copper, iron, and lead, so he said: 'Upon them all is khums.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of khums on mined metals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific categories of ma'adin (minerals) are explicitly listed, confirming that the khums obligation extends beyond precious metals to include base metals like iron and lead. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the financial rights of the state and the Imam on extracted natural resources, distinguishing them from general trade goods.
